core: 把 shifts focus to what happened to an object after an action, not the action itself. Learners often forget to add a result word after the verb, e.g. saying 把饭吃 instead of 把饭吃完.

sentences.situation: At home · to your younger sibling
sentences.pinyin: bǎ mén guān hǎo, wài miàn tài lěng le.
sentences.en: Close the door properly, it's freezing outside.
sentences.why: You tell a family member to make sure the door is fully closed, usually when cold wind or noise is coming in.
sentences.tip: Do not say 把门关 alone; always add a result word like 好 or 上 after the verb.

sentences.zh: 请把这份文件复印一下。
sentences.pinyin: qǐng bǎ zhè fèn wén jiàn fù yìn yī xià.
sentences.en: Please make a copy of this document.
sentences.why: A polite, common request between coworkers for a small routine office task.
sentences.tip: Adding 一下 makes the request sound softer and less demanding.

sentences.zh: 麻烦帮我把这杯咖啡加热一下。
sentences.pinyin: má fán bāng wǒ bǎ zhè bēi kā fēi jiā rè yī xià.
sentences.en: Could you please heat up this coffee for me?
sentences.why: You ask service staff to fix your drink, using 麻烦 to sound polite and not entitled.
sentences.tip: This is much more natural than bluntly saying 把咖啡加热.

sentences.situation: Friend's birthday · to your close friend
sentences.zh: 我把你送我的书看完了，特别好看！
sentences.pinyin: wǒ bǎ nǐ sòng wǒ de shū kàn wán le, tè bié hǎo kàn!
sentences.en: I finished the book you gave me, it was so good!
sentences.why: You tell a friend you completed reading their gift, to show you appreciated their present.
sentences.tip: The 了 at the end marks the action is fully completed.

sentences.situation: Office meeting · team lead to the group
sentences.zh: 大家把下周的报告准备好。
sentences.pinyin: dà jiā bǎ xià zhōu de bào gào zhǔn bèi hǎo.
sentences.en: Everyone please get next week's report ready.
sentences.why: A manager gives a clear work instruction to the whole team, not asking for debate.
sentences.tip: No 请 here, it sounds like a standard work instruction, not a favor.

sentences.zh: 麻烦把我们的菜分开打包。
sentences.pinyin: má fán bǎ wǒ men de cài fēn kāi dǎ bāo.
sentences.en: Could you pack our dishes separately for takeaway?
sentences.why: You ask for leftover takeaway packaging at a restaurant, specifying you want different meals in separate boxes.
sentences.tip: 分开 is the key result word here, meaning 'separately'.

sentences.situation: Family dining table · parent to child
sentences.zh: 快把手机放下，好好吃饭。
sentences.pinyin: kuài bǎ shǒu jī fàng xià, hǎo hǎo chī fàn.
sentences.en: Put your phone down right now, eat your meal properly.
sentences.why: A parent scolds a child for using their phone during dinner, a very common household scenario.
sentences.tip: 快 adds urgency, making the tone sound more strict.

sentences.zh: 我今天加班，你下班记得把快递取回来。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ jīn tiān jiā bān, nǐ xià bān jì de bǎ kuài dì qǔ huí lái.
sentences.en: I'm working overtime today, remember to pick up the package when you get off work.
sentences.why: You send a quick reminder to your roommate to grab your delivered package on their way home.
sentences.tip: 取回来 is the natural phrasal verb for picking up a package from a delivery spot.

sentences.zh: 我已经把方案改好了，您过目。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ yǐ jīng bǎ fāng àn gǎi hǎo le, nín guò mù.
sentences.en: I have already revised the proposal, please take a look.
sentences.why: An employee reports finished work to their boss, using formal respectful language like 您 and 过目.
sentences.tip: 过目 is a polite formal phrase meaning 'please look over my work'.

sentences.zh: 请各部门在周五前把年度总结提交完毕。
sentences.pinyin: qǐng gè bù mén zài zhōu wǔ qián bǎ nián dù zǒng jié tí jiāo wán bì.
sentences.en: All departments must submit the annual summary before Friday.
sentences.why: This is a formal company-wide instruction, using official written language with no casual tone.
sentences.tip: 完毕 is formal written language, you would never use it in daily spoken chat.

quiz.prompt: You are at home, tell your roommate to turn off the lights when they leave the room.
accept: 麻烦走的时候把灯关一下。
走的时候记得把灯关掉。
quiz.explain: This is the natural casual way to ask someone to turn off lights using the 把 structure.

quiz.prompt: You are at a café, politely ask the staff to give you a new spoon for your drink.
quiz.answer: 麻烦帮我把这个勺子换一个新的。
accept: 麻烦帮我换一把新勺子。
请帮我把这个勺子换成新的。
quiz.explain: Using 麻烦 makes the request polite, and 把 clearly focuses on the spoon as the object being changed.

quiz.prompt: You are talking to your close friend, tell them you finished watching the movie they recommended to you, and say it was really good.
quiz.answer: 我把你推荐的那部电影看完了，特别好看！
quiz.explain: 把 is used here to show you completed the action of finishing the movie, which is the key focus of the sentence.

quiz.prompt: You are an employee talking to your manager, tell them you have already sent the project email to the client, politely.
quiz.answer: 我已经把项目邮件发给客户了，您可以看看。
quiz.explain: This formal, polite tone uses 把 to highlight the completed action of sending the email, appropriate for talking to a boss.

quiz.prompt: 你和家人一起吃饭，妈妈说：“你怎么一直看手机？”你要怎么回答，告诉她你马上放下手机好好吃饭？
quiz.answer: 好的妈妈，我马上把手机放下，好好吃饭。
accept: 好，我这就把手机放下，专心吃饭。
我马上把手机收起来，好好吃饭。
quiz.explain: This natural response uses 把 to refer to putting down the phone, matching the casual, apologetic tone when responding to a parent.

quiz.prompt: 你的同事问你：“你昨天要改的报告写完了吗？”你要回答说你已经改完了，现在可以发给领导了。
quiz.answer: 我已经把报告改完了，现在就可以发给领导。
accept: 我把报告改好了，现在就发给他。
我已经把报告修改完了，随时可以发。
quiz.explain: 把 is used here to focus on the completed action of finishing the report, which is the information your colleague is asking about.
